Dual Plates: Crossing the Border Without Stopping Your Operation

  • absolute
  • September 25, 2026
  • 9:40 am
  • No Comments

A border crossing shouldn't be a pause

For any company moving freight between Mexico and the United States, the border is often the most sensitive point of the entire route. It’s where wait times pile up, where cargo changes hands, and where a small delay can turn into a late delivery on the other side.

In many transportation setups, freight arrives at the border in one unit and has to be transferred to another to continue its journey. Every transfer means extra coordination, more time sitting still, and one more link in the chain where something can go wrong.

At Absolute Group, we believe crossing the border shouldn’t mean stopping your operation. That’s why we work with a dual-plate system.

What does operating with dual plates mean?

Our units are equipped with a dual-plate system that allows them to operate legally in Mexico and travel in the United States. In practical terms, the same unit that picks up your freight on one side of the border can continue its route on the other side, without unnecessary interruptions along the way.

This removes one of the most common friction points in cross-border transportation: switching units at the border. Your freight stays in a single unit, with a single carrier responsible for it from start to finish.

Benefits for your freight

Operating with dual plates isn’t just a technical advantage; it’s a difference you’ll see in transit times and in the peace of mind of your operation:

  • Fewer delays — by avoiding transfers at the border, your freight spends less time stopped and more time moving.
  • A more efficient crossing — the unit continues its route without depending on a second carrier being available on the other side.
  • Less cargo handling — fewer unit changes mean less risk of damage, shortages, or documentation errors.
  • One point of accountability — no need to coordinate with multiple providers; your freight stays with Absolute for the entire trip.
  • Continuous visibility — with real-time GPS tracking, you know where your shipment is before, during, and after the crossing.

Technology and operations designed to keep your freight moving

Dual plates work best as part of a complete operation. That’s why we back them with the tools that make every crossing faster and more secure:

  • C-TPAT certification, supporting safe and reliable operations with U.S. customs authorities.
  • PrePass technology, to reduce unnecessary stops at roadside inspection stations.
  • EDI integration, so your shipment data moves as fast as your freight.
  • An owned fleet of 100+ units, handling 800+ shipments per month with coverage across more than 50% of the United States.

Less friction at the border, more control over your supply chain

When your freight doesn’t have to stop to change units, everything else becomes more predictable: delivery times, communication with your customers, and planning for your production or inventory.

At Absolute Group, we’ve designed our operation so the border stops being an obstacle and becomes just one more point along the route.

Absolute Group: The Logistics Partner Your Operation Needs

Since 2011, Absolute Group has grown from a single truck to a fleet of more than 100 units crossing between Mexico and the United States every day. Dual plates, C-TPAT certification, real-time tracking, and a team that understands both sides of the border — all built so your freight arrives on time, with no surprises.

Ready for your freight to cross without stopping? Let’s talk about your next route.

Producing in Mexico, selling in the United States

The model is increasingly common: manufacturing in Mexico, sales and distribution in the United States. It works when the supply chain is well designed, and it grinds to a halt the moment the border crossing becomes a bottleneck.

Reliable cross-border transport isn’t an add-on service within this operation — it’s the piece that keeps everything moving. Without it, every advantage of producing in Mexico gets diluted by delays, third-party transfers, and lost visibility of freight in transit.

The link between both countries

At Absolute Group, we’re the link between Mexico and the United States for companies already operating under this model. With more than 100 units and over 800 shipments a month, we move our clients’ freight with our own fleet, without relying on third-party transfers at the border crossing.

That translates into:

  • Real-time GPS monitoring — full visibility of your shipment from pickup to delivery

Your operation is already in Mexico. We connect it to the U.S.

That’s exactly what we do at Absolute Group every day.

Industries already moving with us

Across all of these, the constant is the same: companies that have already figured out where to produce, and now need to figure out how to move that production into the U.S. market without middlemen or surprises.

Cross-Border Trucking Mexico–U.S.

Grow Without Slowing Down

For many Mexican companies, the U.S. market is the natural next stage of growth. But the border is often seen as a barrier: paperwork, transfers between carriers, idle time, and the uncertainty of not knowing where your freight is for days.

The reality is different. With the right partner, cross-border transportation between Mexico and the United States stops being an obstacle and becomes what it actually is: one more waypoint within your supply chain.

What is cross-border transportation between Mexico and the U.S.?

Cross-border transportation is the service that moves freight from its origin in Mexico to its final destination in the United States (or the other way around), managing the domestic haul, the border crossing, and the haul on U.S. soil.

The difference between good and bad service comes down to how many hands touch the freight along the way. Every transfer to a third party is one more risk: one more delay, one document that doesn’t match, one less clear point of responsibility.

Coverage: freight transportation to more than 80 U.S. cities

Our cross-border transportation network covers more than 80 cities in the United States, with presence in roughly 50% of the country, including the Southwest, Midwest, Southeast, and Northeast regions.

That means your product can reach:

  • The manufacturing and automotive corridors of Texas, Michigan, Ohio, and Indiana.
  • The distribution centers of the Midwest and the Southeast.
  • The consumer markets of the Northeast, including Pennsylvania and New York.

With more than 800 shipments per month, these aren’t routes on paper: they are destinations we run consistently, with known transit times and teams that already know the way.

Real-time tracking: visibility at every mile

In cross-border logistics, trust isn’t built on promises — it’s built on visibility. That’s why our operation runs on technology that keeps your team informed at all times:

  • Real-time GPS monitoring, with online access to the location of every unit.
  • EDI integration for efficient data exchange with your systems.
  • Prepass technology, standard across our entire fleet, to keep trips moving.
  • 24/7 monitoring of trucks and trailers as CTPAT members, from pickup to delivery.

When your team can answer “where is my shipment?” in seconds instead of hours, the entire planning process changes.

What a cross-border trucking company should offer you

Before hiring a carrier for the Mexico–U.S. corridor, make sure it meets the following:

CTPAT certification

Backing its security processes before the customs authorities of both countries.

Direct crossing with no third parties

To avoid transfers that fragment accountability.

With actual access for your team, not just email reports.

With CCTV, reinforced perimeters, and controlled access.

Absolute Group meets every one of these criteria. Our facilities in Laredo, Texas, operate with a closed-circuit CCTV system, reinforced perimeters, controlled access, and alarm systems connected directly to local law enforcement.

How long does a shipment from Mexico to the United States take?

It depends on the origin, the destination, and the crossing point. By running direct crossings with no third-party transfers, we eliminate the most costly waits in the process and keep transit times predictable.

What is CTPAT certification and why does it matter?

CTPAT is a binational program that certifies companies whose operations meet the highest security standards in the supply chain. A certified carrier reduces the likelihood of additional inspections and speeds up the crossing.

Which industries do you serve?

We work primarily with companies in manufacturing, automotive, electronics, industrial equipment, and retail — handling both time-critical components and finished products.

Since 2011 we have grown from a single truck to more than 200 units operating between Mexico and the United States, with presence in over 80 cities and more than 800 shipments delivered every month. Whether you need door-to-door service, border crossing, expedited service, or warehousing and cross-docking, we have the coverage and the experience to move your freight with confidence.

A border crossing shouldn't be a bottleneck

CTPAT: The Certification That Lets Your Freight Cross With Confidence

When freight reaches the border between Mexico and the United States, every minute of waiting can mean delays on the production line, late deliveries, or costs no one planned for. At Absolute Group, we understand that a border crossing shouldn’t be the point where your supply chain stops — it should be the point where it keeps moving.

That’s why our CTPAT (Customs-Trade Partnership Against Terrorism) certification isn’t just a plaque on our office wall. It’s the foundation behind faster, safer, and more predictable crossings for every one of our clients.

What is CTPAT certification, and why does it matter?

CTPAT is a binational program that certifies transportation companies whose operations meet the highest security standards in the supply chain. Not just any carrier gets it — it requires submitting processes, facilities, and personnel to a rigorous evaluation by customs authorities.

Holding this certification means:

  • Authorities on both sides of the border already recognize and validate our security processes.
  • Our tractors and trailers operate under 24/7 monitoring, from pickup to final delivery.
  • Our facilities include CCTV, reinforced perimeters, and controlled access at all times.
  • Your freight is less likely to be flagged for additional inspections at the crossing.

In other words: when you work with a CTPAT-certified company, you’re not just trusting us — you’re trusting a process that authorities have already backed.

A faster crossing, with no middlemen

Thanks to our certification and to operating the border crossing with our own fleet — with no need for third-party transfers — we make sure your freight moves between Mexico and the United States (and back) with less friction and greater predictability.

That translates into:

  • Lower operational risk, backed by our full monitoring system and 24-hour CCTV network.
  • More predictable processes — essential for manufacturing, automotive, and retail companies that can't afford an improvised supply chain.

Trust as a competitive advantage

Choosing a CTPAT-certified carrier isn’t just another box to check on your vendor list — it’s a decision that directly impacts the efficiency of your operation. A faster crossing means more on-time deliveries, fewer hidden costs from delays, and a logistics partner that authorities on both sides of the border already recognize as reliable.

At Absolute Group, we work every day to make sure that level of trust shows up in every crossing, every shipment, and every delivery — whether it’s a one-time shipment or a large-scale, recurring operation.

Our Fleet

THE CAPACITY THAT MAKES THE DIFFERENCE IN EVERY SHIPMENT

When your freight deserves reliable transportation, every detail counts. Trailer size, load capacity, and equipment condition aren’t minor details — they’re the factors that determine whether your cargo arrives complete, on time, and without setbacks. At Absolute Group, we know this, which is why we’ve built a fleet designed to meet the real needs of our clients, regardless of volume or operational complexity.

53-Foot Dry Van Trailers: Space Built for Your Operation

Our 53-foot dry van trailers offer capacity for up to 26 pallets and 20 tons of cargo, giving you the space your operation needs without sacrificing security or delivery times. This type of equipment is ideal for companies moving significant volumes between Mexico and the United States that require consistency, shipment after shipment.

Whether your freight is part of a manufacturing, retail, or distribution operation, having the right amount of space means fewer trips, less handling of your merchandise, and a more efficient supply chain from start to finish. A trailer with the right capacity also reduces the risk of damage from excessive handling and optimizes cost per unit shipped — something that directly impacts your operation’s margin.

What Type of Freight Is Best Suited for a 53-Foot Dry Van?

Not all freight requires the same type of equipment, and choosing correctly from the start avoids delays and extra costs. Our dry van trailers are the right choice when your cargo:

  • Doesn't require refrigeration, but does need full protection from weather, dust, and humidity
  • Needs additional safeguarding against theft or mishandling during transit
  • Moves in high volumes on a recurring basis between Mexico and the U.S.
  • Includes finished goods, industrial supplies, electronics, textiles, or consumer products

Thanks to its enclosed design and capacity of up to 20 tons, this type of trailer works for both consolidated shipments and full truckload freight, without compromising the integrity of what you’re transporting.

 

Security That Backs Every Pallet

Load capacity only holds value when it’s backed by real security. Our operations yard features 24-hour CCTV surveillance, reinforced perimeters, and alarm systems connected directly to local authorities — all designed so your merchandise is protected from pickup to final delivery, not just during transit.

This infrastructure, combined with our Door 2 Door approach, allows us to manage drayage in Mexico, the border crossing, and the U.S. operation under a single provider, with one point of contact and no surprises in cost or timing.

FAQs

How many tons can a 53-foot dry van trailer carry?

Our units have capacity for up to 20 tons of cargo — enough for manufacturing, retail, and distribution operations that move significant volumes on a recurring basis.

How many pallets fit in a 53-foot trailer?

Up to 26 standard pallets, depending on how the cargo is arranged and the type of product being shipped.

Does a dry van protect cargo from weather and humidity?

Yes. Being a fully enclosed trailer, it offers complete protection against rain, dust, humidity, and temperature changes throughout the entire trip.

Can I ship consolidated freight, or only full truckloads?

Both. Our dry van fleet handles both consolidated shipments and full truckload (TL) freight, depending on your volume and shipping frequency.

What happens if my cargo crosses the Mexico–United States border?

We operate under a Door 2 Door model, with direct border crossing, no third-party transfers, real-time GPS monitoring, and C-TPAT-certified security throughout the entire route.

The difference between reliable transportation

and one that creates problems usually comes down to the questions you ask before hiring it.

When your freight crosses the border, you’re not just hiring a truck: you’re entrusting your operation, your delivery times, and your customer relationships to a third party. A careless choice can translate into customs delays, loss of visibility over your cargo, and costs you never accounted for in your budget.

The good news is that most of these problems can be anticipated. It’s enough to ask the right questions before signing. These are the ones that truly protect your operation.

1. Is the border crossing direct, or does it rely on third parties?

Every handoff between carriers is a point where your freight can stall, get lost, or lose traceability. A direct border-crossing model eliminates those handoffs and keeps your cargo under a single point of control from origin to destination.

At Absolute Group, we operate with a dual-plate system that streamlines crossings and lets us closely monitor every load throughout the entire trip, without handing it off to intermediaries.

2. Will I have real-time tracking of my freight transportation?

Knowing where your cargo is at all times isn’t a luxury: it’s the foundation for making decisions, keeping your customers informed, and reacting in time if something changes. Always ask whether the carrier offers online GPS tracking and direct access to that information.

Our fleet features real-time GPS monitoring and Prepass technology as standard, along with EDI integration for a smooth flow of information between your company and ours.

Traceability isn’t an extra: it’s the foundation for anticipating delays and making decisions with room to spare. Knowing where the cargo is at all times lets you keep your customers informed and respond before an unexpected event turns into a problem.

What sustains an operation in control:

  • Real-time GPS tracking throughout the entire route
  • EDI integration for a smooth flow of information
  • Prepass technology as standard to speed up crossings
  • Solid customs processes, with no improvisation

3. Will you support me with customs documentation?

An error in the paperwork can hold your freight at the border for hours or days. Support with customs documentation and a well-coordinated process on both sides makes the difference between an on-time delivery and a costly delay.

With our Door 2 Door model, we manage the drayage in Mexico, the border crossing, and the operation in the United States as a single process, coordinated by an expert team.

Customs documentation and door-to-door process

An error in the paperwork or a fragmented process can hold cargo for hours or days. With our Door 2 Door model, we manage the drayage in Mexico, the border crossing, customs documentation support, and the operation in the United States as a single process coordinated by an expert team. This reduces risk and optimizes costs by avoiding hidden charges at every stage.

4. What security measures back up my cargo?

Security doesn’t end when the truck leaves the yard. Ask about certifications, monitoring, and protocols. As CTPAT members, we maintain 24/7 monitoring of trucks and trailers, along with yards equipped with live CCTV, reinforced perimeters, and controlled access.

Security that doesn't stop at the yard

Cargo protection must be constant, from pickup to delivery. As CTPAT members, we maintain 24/7 monitoring of trucks and trailers, yards with live CCTV, reinforced perimeters, and controlled access. Well-structured security doesn’t react to the incident: it prevents it.

5. Does the price reflect the complete service?

The lowest cost isn’t always the most convenient. A fragmented model can hide additional charges at every stage. A comprehensive service, on the other hand, optimizes costs by managing the entire route under a single point of control.

The difference shows in the results

Not all transportation companies operate to the same standard. Some only manage shipments and respond to setbacks as they come; others design complete operations with direct crossing, real-time visibility, customs support, and reinforced security to sustain continuity even when the market gets demanding. The difference lies in real capacity and advance planning, not in last-minute promises. At Absolute, we work to ensure your freight reaches its destination with the security and control your business needs.

The 3 Questions You Should Ask Before Hiring a Cross-Border Transportation Provider

  • absolute
  • June 19, 2026
  • 1:13 pm
  • No Comments

The Right Questions

Before Hiring a Cross-Border Transportation Provider

In the Mexico–United States trade environment, almost any carrier can claim to be “reliable.” The real difference shows up when you ask the right questions before signing, not after your cargo is already in transit. Companies that avoid delays, loss of visibility, and unnecessary costs are the ones that screen their providers with clear criteria from the very first contact.

Why the Right Questions Protect Your Operation

Choosing a carrier based on price or immediate availability is the most common way to end up with surprises in the middle of a crossing. The lowest rate rarely includes, in writing, what truly determines a shipment’s outcome: how the border is crossed, how much visibility you have into the journey, and how prepared the carrier is when it comes to customs. These variables almost never appear on the quote, but they’re the ones that end up costing time and money when something doesn’t go as planned. Choosing an experienced Cross-Border Transportation provider helps reduce these risks from the start.

Direct border crossing, real-time tracking, and support with customs documentation aren’t premium extras; they’re the factors that determine whether your cargo arrives on time or your team spends the day calling around trying to find out where it is. An operation without these elements depends on luck; an operation that has them depends on processes, and processes are what you can actually control. Reliable Cross-Border Transportation is built on these processes, ensuring consistency and visibility throughout every shipment.

Before hiring, there are three questions that mark the difference between a transportation provider and a true logistics partner:

  • Is the border crossing direct, or does it require transfers with third parties?
  • Can I monitor my cargo in real time throughout the entire journey?
  • Do they have experience and proven support in customs documentation?

Direct Border Crossing: No Transfers, No Surprises

Every cargo transfer between carriers is a point where something can go wrong: delays, damage, loss of control over how your merchandise is handled. A provider with a direct border crossing eliminates that risk because the same operation covers the Mexican leg, the crossing, and the U.S. leg, without handing your cargo off to third parties along the way. This is one of the biggest advantages of reliable Cross-Border Transportation.

At Absolute Group, we operate with a “double plate” system that enables efficient crossings and keeps our own team in control of the client’s cargo throughout the entire journey, from start to finish. Expected Regulatory Shifts:

What Is LMCA?

The Laredo Motor Carriers Association is a respected nonprofit group that unites motor carriers, logistics companies, and transportation professionals operating throughout the Laredo region.

Its mission is to:

  • Promote safety standards in the transportation industry
  • Strengthen the professional community of carriers
  • Support drivers through training, education, and advocacy
  • Create opportunities for networking and collaboration
  • Foster positive relationships between transportation companies and local agencies

Because Laredo handles billions of dollars in cross-border trade every year, the association plays a key role in maintaining efficiency, security, and compliance within the region’s logistics ecosystem.
